research.statement: A lane's pool is a THIRD surface: an arm can be named by the order, absent from the lane's pool, and still reachable provider-direct on the same relay.
research.evidence: dispatch_r10.py VERIFY_SECURITY -> exit 4, code ERR_LANE_REQUIRED_ARM_ABSENT, identity_gate.arms=[rank1 openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol], dispatcher text 'the required arm is not in this lane's pool'; the same model+provider returned PROBE_OK on a one-shot smoke probe

research.statement: The dispatcher's nonce gate reads fewer surfaces than the receipt it writes: it parses transcript agent_message events while the same receipt records a stdout file (429,783 bytes) and a stdout_tail string that both contain the nonce.
research.evidence: VERIFY_SECURITY_dispatch_receipt_attempt1.json: code ERR_NO_ARM_EMITTED_NONCE, nonce_present false, nonce_source item.completed/agent_message; the nonce appears in that receipt's own stdout_tail and in the recorded stdout_path

research.statement: A role-scoped receipt path destroyed provenance for 11 attempt-1 turns in one session (7 EXECUTE, 4 VERIFY_SECURITY), i.e. up to 9 receipts destroyed; the round first recorded 8 and an independent checker corrected the magnitude.
research.evidence: the independent checker's raw listing (R10_VERIFY/raw/t1b_pytest_live.txt, t1c_turn_mapping.txt) plus the surviving file's mtime/content; the direction was already measured by this round, the magnitude was understated

research.statement: check_drift == [] does NOT imply the registry is internally consistent: it compares each projection pointer with its own target, so a registry can read drift-free while check_sod reports SOD_VIOLATION for a declared-distinct pair (measured: PLAN and VERIFY_SECURITY both resolving to openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol).

A 0-byte reading of a live file is a PROBE result, never a corruption finding - but the mechanism must not be guessed either. Measured: the file is 35739 bytes now; the tree's own write log shows NO write in the probe's read window and shows its current digest created at 13:35:06 by a DIFFERENT session, and the previous content digest (8af86f502767) has no copy on this host - so the past state is NOT re-measurable and this round's 'loader rewrite race' explanation is WITHDRAWN.
research.evidence: refuted reading + corrected attribution; checker disagreements D3/D4 (R10_VERIFY/R10_VERDICT.json)

research.statement: A change record is not updated by the act that performs its work: 20 rows of one record were fully DONE in the live system while the record read 0/25.
research.evidence: the registry carries the rebind the record asks for (epoch 21, admission ADMITTED) while tasks.md was untouched

learning.lesson: Before dispatching a mandated arm, read the LANE's own pool (or the dispatcher's identity_gate), not only the registry: an arm absent from the pool fail-closes as a routing absence, not a model outage.
Keep four attribution surfaces separate in every statement - declared (registry), pooled (identity_gate), reachable (provider-direct), served (attempts[]). Never let one stand for another.
Never edit the route registry or the lane slots so that your own dispatch can succeed; run the mandated model provider-direct and disclose the deviation, or fail closed and report.
Treat a change record as a CLAIM about state, not as state: measure the system before adjudicating a row, and never tick a row whose artifact you have not seen.
A reader that confirms a value must be re-run twice, or hashed, when a loader is known to rewrite files: single reads can race a rewrite and manufacture a false alarm about the subject.
Publish the TESTED REVISION (bytes+sha256) with any test result; an artifact can change while it is being verified, and a verdict that names no revision cannot be reproduced.
When a claim about the PAST cannot be re-measured, say NOT RE-MEASURABLE and stop; do not supply a plausible mechanism (a loader race) that the write log does not support.
